title: Friendship
lead: The Bible prizes the friend who stays loyal in hard days and warns against the friend who turns. Proverbs and Ben Sira give practical rules for keeping friends; David and Jonathan show friendship at its deepest; God calls Abraham his friend; Jesus calls his disciples friends and lays down his life for them.

sections.b: Proverbs says, "At every time a friend keeps loving, / and a brother is born for the hard days" (Proverbs 17:17), and warns that a crowd of friends is not the same as one who holds on "tighter than a brother" (Proverbs 18:24). Jonathan loved David "as much as his own life" (1 Samuel 18:1). The betrayal of a friend is one of the Psalms' deepest griefs: "the one I trusted, / who ate my bread, / has raised his heel high against me" (Psalm 41:9), words Jesus applies to Judas (John 13:18). Abraham "was called the friend of God" (James 2:23; compare Isaiah 41:8), and the LORD spoke to Moses "as anyone talks with a close companion" (Exodus 33:11). Jesus gives friendship its fullest meaning: "There is no greater love anyone can have than this: to lay down his life for the sake of his friends" (John 15:13). Wisdom literature adds practical rules. "Wounds from someone who loves you are true" (Proverbs 27:6), and "a person sharpens his friend's face" (Proverbs 27:17). Ecclesiastes counts the worth of a companion: "if they fall, one of them raises his companion" (Ecclesiastes 4:10). Job complains that his friends failed him when he needed them: "My brothers have betrayed me like a wadi" (Job 6:15). Jesus tells his disciples, "I have called you friends" (John 15:15), and James warns that "being the world's friend means being God's enemy" (James 4:4).

sections.b: Sirach, a book in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles, returns to friendship again and again: testing a new friend and the worth of a faithful one (Sirach 6:5-17), quarrels that can be mended and betrayals that cannot (Sirach 22:19-26), the friend who tells secrets (Sirach 27:16-21) and false friends (Sirach 37:1-6). "A faithful friend is a solid roof over you, / and the man who has found him has found treasure" (Sirach 6:14). The Sirach passages are gathered below.
